Getting started with rgeodesy

Source: vignettes/rgeodesy.Rmd
rgeodesy.Rmd
library(rgeodesy)

rgeodesy wraps Rust Geodesy (RG), a platform for experiments with geodetic transformations. A transformation is a pipeline string of named operators; you apply it to vectors of coordinates.

The core idea: pipelines, not CRS codes

Unlike PROJ, RG does not take EPSG codes or a from -> to pair of coordinate reference systems. You spell out the transformation as a pipeline of operator primitives chained with |, each taking key=value arguments. For example, projecting geographic coordinates to UTM zone 32:

geod_apply("gis:in | utm zone=32", x = 12, y = 55)
#> $x
#> [1] 691875.6
#> 
#> $y
#> [1] 6098908

Coordinate order and units

RG works internally in radians with a geodetic (latitude-first) axis order, so geographic data is bracketed with an I/O adaptor that converts units and order:

  • gis:in / gis:out — degrees in GIS order (lon, lat), i.e. the natural (x, y) order. Recommended for most R users.
  • geo:in / geo:out — degrees in geodetic order (lat, lon).

These two give the same result when you swap the arguments:

geod_apply("gis:in | utm zone=55 south", x = 147.3, y = -42.9)
#> $x
#> [1] 524492.1
#> 
#> $y
#> [1] 5250246
geod_apply("geo:in | utm zone=55 south", x = -42.9, y = 147.3)
#> $x
#> [1] 524492.1
#> 
#> $y
#> [1] 5250246

Inverse transformations

Pass inv = TRUE to run a pipeline backwards. Applying the forward pipeline and then its inverse recovers the input:

fwd <- geod_apply("gis:in | utm zone=55 south", x = 147.3, y = -42.9)
fwd
#> $x
#> [1] 524492.1
#> 
#> $y
#> [1] 5250246
geod_apply("gis:in | utm zone=55 south", x = fwd$x, y = fwd$y, inv = TRUE)
#> $x
#> [1] 147.3
#> 
#> $y
#> [1] -42.9

Matrix output

geod_xy() returns a two-column matrix instead of a list, which is handy for feeding into other spatial code:

geod_xy("gis:in | utm zone=55 south",
        x = c(147.3, 147.5),
        y = c(-42.9, -42.8))
#>             x       y
#> [1,] 524492.1 5250246
#> [2,] 540886.1 5261273

Validating pipelines

geod_validate() compiles a pipeline and returns TRUE, or an error string if it cannot be built — useful for checking user input before applying it:

geod_validate("gis:in | utm zone=55 south")
#> [1] TRUE
geod_validate("utm zone=banana")
#> [1] "Malformed value for parameter 'zone': 'banana'"

A malformed pipeline passed to geod_apply() raises a normal R error:

geod_apply("utm zone=banana", x = 1, y = 1)
#> Error in `geod_apply()`:
#> ! Failed to build op 'utm zone=banana': Malformed value for parameter 'zone': 'banana'

What’s available

geod_ops() lists every registered operator and adaptor. See vignette("operators") for a tour of the transformation families.

head(geod_ops(), 20)
#>  [1] "adapt"       "addone"      "axisswap"    "btmerc"      "butm"       
#>  [6] "cart"        "curvature"   "deflection"  "deformation" "dm"         
#> [11] "dms"         "enu:in"      "enu:out"     "geo:in"      "geo:out"    
#> [16] "geodesic"    "gis:in"      "gis:out"     "gravity"     "gridshift"
length(geod_ops())
#> [1] 44
